decision_description: Constitutional compliance check of docs/tier5_deliverables/review_packets/review_packet.json (schema_id: orch.tier5.review_packet.v1, run_id: 531ec9f0-26bc-4906-9197-3b604352d011) identified four violations: §13.2 (call constraints asserted without Tier 2B source tracing — HRS4R label exemption, CoARA alignment requirement, and verbatim evaluation sub-criterion text cited as call mandates without reference to docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/); §13.3 (project facts asserted without Tier 3 source tracing — named individuals Dr. Rositsa Cholakova and Dr. András Jung, institution ELTE, associated partner AgroVIR, and specific work package/task/deliverable/risk identifiers WP3, WP4, T3-02, T3-03, T5-02, D3-01, D5-02, RISK-06, KPI-01, KPI-05, KPI-06, claim C-03 appear without primary_sources[] references to docs/tier3_project_instantiation/); §13.9 (Horizon Europe programme-rule claims including the European Charter for Researchers, HRS4R, and CoARA are asserted from agent-local knowledge without reference to Tier 1 normative framework documents in docs/tier1_normative_framework/extracted/); §13.10 (Tier 5 artifact entirely lacks traceability_footer field, primary_sources[] array, and no_unsupported_claims_declaration, making no material claim in the artifact traceable to a specific Tier 1–4 input). Three violations are classified critical; one (§13.9) is classified major. Human operator resolution is required before the review packet can be treated as a constitutionally compliant Tier 5 output. The review findings themselves (F-001 through F-006) and revision actions (A-1 through A-6) are substantively sound; the violations arise entirely from the absence of the structural traceability fields mandated for Tier 5 artifacts.
alternatives_considered: Accept review packet as constitutionally compliant on grounds that review packets are operationally distinct from proposal section artifacts and traceability footer requirements apply only to proposal prose — rejected because CLAUDE.md §13.10 and §11.4 apply to all Tier 5 outputs without category exemption; orch.tier5.review_packet.v1 is explicitly a Tier 5 artifact.

Treat the violations as minor and defer recording to a post-remediation entry — rejected because CLAUDE.md §9.4 requires durable recording of decisions affecting future interpretation, and three critical violations affecting a Phase 8 gate artifact require immediate durable recording per §13.5.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §13 — specifically §13.2 (inventing call constraints not present in Tier 2B), §13.3 (inventing project facts not present in Tier 3), §13.9 (substituting agent-local programme knowledge for Tier 1 source documents), and §13.10 (producing Tier 5 outputs not traceable to specific Tier 1–4 inputs); cross-referenced with CLAUDE.md §11.4 (Tier 5 content must be derivable from Tier 1–4 state and must not introduce facts not grounded in a higher tier) and §12.2 (validation status vocabulary requiring named source attribution for Confirmed evidence).
rationale: The constitutional compliance check skill (report_id: compliance_check_review_packet_evaluator_reviewer_2026-07-30T120000Z) executed a systematic §13 prohibition scan over review_packet.json. The artifact's traceability infrastructure is entirely absent: no traceability_footer field exists in the artifact at any level, meaning none of the material claims in the six findings (F-001 through F-006) or six revision actions (A-1 through A-6) carry any source attribution to Tier 1–4 documents. This structural omission simultaneously triggers §13.2 (MSCA-specific evaluation sub-criteria including HRS4R and CoARA cited as call mandates without Tier 2B extraction references), §13.3 (project-specific entities and identifiers named without Tier 3 source confirmation), §13.9 (European Charter for Researchers and HRS4R procedural detail derived from programme knowledge rather than Tier 1 documents), and §13.10 (Tier 5 artifact with no traceable pathway to Tier 1–4 inputs). The four violations do not arise from the substantive quality of the review findings — the evaluation criteria coverage gaps identified in F-001 through F-006 and the revision prioritisation in A-1 through A-6 are methodologically sound — but from the absence of the traceability apparatus required of all Tier 5 deliverables. Remediation requires: (1) extending the orch.tier5.review_packet.v1 schema to include a traceability_footer with primary_sources[] referencing applicable Tier 2A evaluation form documents, Tier 2B scope_requirements.json and expected_outcomes.json, and Tier 3 sources for all named project entities; (2) regenerating the review packet with those references populated; and (3) adding a no_unsupported_claims_declaration consistent with the sourcing level achieved. Until remediation is complete and a compliant review packet is produced, the current artifact must not be treated as a constitutionally valid Tier 5 output.
